en.html:
By the time our feet reached Enoshima, the night was already well past its middle. First, arrange a small boat. Then, manage the small boat with our very small experience. In these two activities the hours had gone. A few more, and dawn would be here.

A small boat. Such a reassuring expression. As though reducing the boat also reduces the skill required to operate it. By that reasoning, give an infant a small sword and send him to war. Chhota hai, sambhal lega. Small only, he will manage. The sea, unfortunately, does not become a smaller sea to accommodate the beginner.

Tonight, a preliminary look only. The full circuit of the island—leave that ambition. Even a look at the shogunate laboratory was probably beyond us.

We were keeping out of sight, so naturally conversation was limited. But suppose this had been a picnic. Then also, would lively chatter have come? Doubtful.

Nobody said it. Nobody needed to. Surely all of us had noticed already. This feeling of nothing—on the skin it was too cold to overlook.

No sign of life.

No animals.

Wild creatures have sharp senses; they do not generally come out to introduce themselves to humans. That much, fine. But no distant scurrying, no faint breath, not even a wary eye on the intruders? Kuch bhi nahi?

Enoshima, where the environment was supposed to be protected with such care. Here, this condition.
What was going on?

なかった。

この体たらく。
　何事であろうか。
